moat_against: #3 in scale behind TJX and Ross — less buying leverage, and recent traffic comparisons show Ross gaining share head-to-head
No customer switching costs or network effects; the assortment is bought, not owned
Adjusted EBIT margin ~8.0% trails larger off-price peers — the scale disadvantage shows in profitability
Tariff exposure on imported merchandise sold to a price-sensitive $25k-$100k income customer
No e-commerce channel of consequence; roic_proxy is null in fundamentals.json, so no computed ROIC history supports a higher score
moat_for: Opportunistic buying organization with a reserve-inventory chase model (in-season buying flexibility)
Structural share tailwind as department stores shrink and off-price takes their share
Opportunistic real estate: bankruptcy-acquired leases and a smaller ~25k sq ft format at low cost
Gross margin expanding five years (41.59% FY2022 to 43.83% FY2026, fundamentals.json) with adjusted EBIT margin expanding
Store runway: 1,287 stores toward a stated 2,000-store target at ~110-115 net new stores a year
moat_justification: A real but replicable buying organization and a long store runway, against larger scaled rivals (TJX, Ross), no switching costs, no pricing power, mid-pack low-40s gross margins, and no computable ROIC series (roic_proxy null in fundamentals.json) to prove returns above the cost of capital through a cycle.
name: Burlington Stores, Inc.
one_liner: Growing, margin-expanding off-price #3, moat 4/10 — but ~$1B/yr of growth capex crushes owner's earnings to a 1.75% yield, so at $260.19 it does not clear 15% on any scored basis (weighted IRR 5.13%, IV@15% $51.05; clears 15% only at $51.05).
